;Arts and culture
*[[92nd Academy Awards]]
**At this year's [[Academy Awards|Oscars]], [[Cinema of South Korea|South Korean]] film ''[[Parasite (2019 film)|Parasite]]'' wins the most awards, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] and [[Academy Award for Best International Feature Film|Best International Film]]. It becomes the first foreign-language film to win Best Picture. [https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lists/oscar-winners-2020-updating-live-full-list-1275973/item/director-1275980 (''The Hollywood Reporter'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Storm Ciara]]
**Winds gusting up to 100 miles per hour have been recorded over much of the [[United Kingdom]] and [[Ireland]], causing widespread damage and disruption. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-51433870 (BBC News)]
**Thousands of homes and businesses have been flooded across [[northern England]] after Storm Ciara brought sustained heavy rainfall to the region. Worst affected were the [[Calder Valley]] settlements of [[Todmorden]], [[Hebden Bridge]] and [[Mytholmroyd]] in [[Yorkshire]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-51433870 (BBC News)]
**A man in [[Hampshire]] was killed when a tree fell onto his car on the [[A33 road]] as a result of high winds. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-51439152 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The death toll of the coronavirus outbreak surpasses the death toll of the [[2002–2004 SARS outbreak]], at 910 deaths. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/09/coronavirus-global-death-toll-overtakes-sars-epidemic (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/china-virus-death-toll-surges-800-infections-mount-200209003721741.html (Al Jazeera)]

;International relations
*[[Cross-Strait relations]]
**[[Taiwan]] scrambles its [[Republic of China Air Force|air force]] to intercept [[People's Liberation Army Air Force|Chinese jets]] after they circled the island during a combat drill. The drill is denounced by the [[Ministry of National Defense (Republic of China)|Taiwanese Defense Ministry]] as a violation of its sovereignty. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-taiwan-china-defence/taiwan-scrambles-armed-jets-as-chinese-air-force-flies-around-island-idUSKBN2030AE (Reuters)]
*[[Israel–Palestine relations]]
**Israel blocks all Palestinian export of agricultural products from the occupied West Bank following Palestinian limitations on imports of Israeli cattle. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/israel-blocks-palestinian-agricultural-exports-jordan-200209104227779.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-to-bar-palestinians-from-exporting-produce-via-jordan-as-trade-war-escalates-1.8506459 (''Haaretz'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Azerbaijani parliamentary election]]
**[[Azerbaijan]] holds a [[snap election]] after [[President of Azerbaijan|President]] [[Ilham Aliyev]] dissolved the [[National Assembly (Azerbaijan)|National Assembly]] last December. The opposition accuses Aliyev of limiting their ability to campaign, and calls for boycotts against the election. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-azerbaijan-election/azeri-president-moves-to-modernize-parliament-with-snap-election-idUSKBN2020S9 (Reuters)]  [https://www.france24.com/en/20200209-azerbaijan-holds-elections-decried-as-sham-by-opposition (France24)]
*[[2020 Cameroonian parliamentary election]]
**After having been postponed twice, [[Elections in Cameroon|parliamentary elections]] are held in [[Cameroon]]. The ongoing [[Anglophone Crisis]] overshadows the process, with supporters of [[Ambazonia]] calling for a boycott of the election. [https://www.dw.com/en/cameroon-elections-a-vote-marked-by-violence-and-abstention/a-52304640 (DW)]
*[[2020 Irish general election]]
**Counting of the first preference votes show [[Sinn Féin]] leading with 24.1% of the vote, ahead of ruling party [[Fine Gael]] and main opposition party [[Fianna Fáil]], each with 22.1%. Sinn Féin leader [[Mary Lou McDonald]] claims victory, declaring that Ireland "is no longer a two-party system", and hopes to form a coalition government. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/09/sinn-fein-to-try-to-form-ruling-coalition-after-irish-election-success (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2020 Swiss referendums]], [[LGBT rights in Switzerland]]
**[[Switzerland|Swiss]] voters head to the polls to vote on a proposal to mandate quotas for affordable housing in new residential development projects, and whether to criminalize discrimination on the basis of [[sexual orientation]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-51370820 (BBC News)] [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/world/europe/switzerland-is-putting-its-housing-crisis-to-a-referendum-1.4155510 (''Irish Times'')]
** The proposal to mandate quotas is rejected, the proposal to criminalize discrimination on the basis of [[sexual orientation]] passes. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-51370820 (BBC News)]
*[[President of El Salvador]] [[Nayib Bukele]] breaks into the [[Legislative Assembly of El Salvador|Legislative Assembly]] with the Army and occupies the chair of the Speaker to demand the approval of a financial measure which couldn't pass earlier as there was no quorum. In a public release, the Presidency department calls for calm after a "demand of insurrection". The opposition accuses the president and the army of intimidation and a "[[self-coup]]". [https://elpais.com/internacional/2020/02/10/america/1581294344_999638.html (''El País'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-51439020 (BBC News)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/el-salvador-standoff-deepens-over-loan-for-security-forces/2020/02/09/1eb51fb6-4b97-11ea-967b-e074d302c7d4_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2020/02/09/world/americas/ap-lt-bc-el-salvador-loan-standoff.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Science and technology
*The [[United Launch Alliance]] successfully launches the [[European Space Agency]]'s [[Solar Orbiter]] (SolO) satellite from [[Cape Canaveral Air Force Station]]. The probe will study the [[Sun]], and in particular its inner [[heliosphere]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-51420402 (BBC News)]
